To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 18 scales are essentially uncorrelated.
( a ) the CPI can be reduced to four factors, and ( b ) the factors are not identical to the 18 CPI scales.
(1) The CPI is not a unidimensional measure of personality, (2) the four factors identified in our research are not orthogonal to each other, and (3) the CPI is not a homogeneous instrument.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of the number of independent dimensions of personality which are measured by the 18 CPI scales.

the question of whether the four factors identified in the previous study are sufficiently independent to warrant the development of a short form CPI, which could then be administered to larger groups of people than are now possible.
the question of how many essentially uncorrelated variables underly the 18 CPI scales, and what the nature of the underlying factors might be.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our earlier results were not conclusive.
the CPI is a multidimensional instrument.
the four factors extracted from the CPI data were not entirely orthogonal, but were sufficiently independent for the purposes of the study to be considered essentially orthogonal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the CPI scales can be reduced to a four-factor structure which, in turn, can be interpreted as a measure of adjustment to social conformity, social poise, superego strength, and capacity for independent thought and action.
the CPI measures four distinct but correlated dimensions of personality, and that these dimensions are essentially uncorrelated.
the CPI measures are highly intercorrelated but not to the point of obliterating the possibility of factor analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CPI is a multidimensional instrument and that its scales are highly correlated.
there are a limited number of factors that underlie the 18 CPI scales.
there is a need to examine the structure of the CPI more thoroughly and in greater depth.
